brief: Cembalest answers foreboding-themed client questions from a West Coast trip. California shows AI-driven growth (3.6% GDP growth, third-highest among states) despite high energy costs and unemployment. On AI concentration: a 42-stock basket drives 60-80% of S&P earnings growth, returns and capex since January 2024; 60% of S&P 500 names sit 20%+ below highs and only 30% outperform the index. He argues this is less fragile than it looks because tech gains come from earnings growth, not multiple expansion, and because corporate profits have so far resisted higher short rates. On federal debt, the 10-year yield has broken Bessent's "Maginot Line" on sticky inflation, hyperscaler issuance and strong GDP, not debt monetization; the deficit tops 5% of GDP for the first time since 1970, and the CBO projects all revenue consumed by entitlements and interest by 2030-31, so he expects budget restructuring over monetization. Private credit stress estimates range from ~5% (Cliffwater) to ~15% (JPM's own BDC measure) despite realized losses near 1-2%. He also covers Anthropic's "abliteration" of a rival open model to push regulation, and Chinese EV share gains in Europe despite tariffs.
